notes.text: Reversal without a stack. Run right to the ⊣ endmarker printing nothing, then walk back left printing each symbol as you pass it. Reading the tape backwards is all the machine needs — no memory beyond the current state.

Compare with the pushdown transducer example, which reverses the same words using a stack and ε-moves. Both compute w ↦ wᴿ; the 2DFT gets there with a finite state set and a head that can turn around, which is why reversal is a REGULAR transduction rather than a genuinely context-free one.

meta.title: Classic: reverse the input
meta.blurb: Scans right in silence, then prints on the way back — computing w ↦ wᴿ with a finite state set and a two-way head, no stack required.
